public_rationale: GovInfoSecurity (ISMG) reports that in the Elloe AI Lab-led study, 94% of agents that keep memory across sessions were vulnerable to poisoning attacks. It also reports that nearly 90% of tested agents drifted from their original goals after roughly 30 steps. Both match Marcus's figures. Wallstreetcn gives the exact numbers, 89.4% and 94%. No source gives different values for these statistics. The paper itself was not found, so this rests on news reports of its findings.
limitations: Primary paper not available; based on news reports.
The exact 89.4% figure appears only in a report that may draw on Marcus's post. ISMG gives 'nearly 90%'.
The study's methods were not verified.

statement.excerpt: Additionally, in the new study 89.4% of agents showed drift relative to their goals after about 30 steps in their process, and 94% of agents with some form of memory-augmentation were vulnerable to poisoning attacks.

our_interpretation: This claim reports the study's findings. It holds if the study reported about 89.4% (nearly 90%) of agents drifting from goals after roughly 30 steps, and 94% of memory-augmented agents vulnerable to poisoning.
A reputable news report of the paper's findings counts as evidence when the paper is unavailable.
criteria.support_condition: The study, or a reliable report of it, gives roughly 89.4% goal drift after about 30 steps and 94% poisoning vulnerability among memory-augmented agents.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The study, or a reliable report of it, gives materially different figures for either statistic, or does not report them.
